timing: Editorial cue timings retained from the original animation; English narration is a translation and is not aligned to a recorded voice.

cues.narration: We identify what a material is made of by studying how it affects light passing through it.
cues.visual: Light passes through a sample and a prism; absorption lines match one of three schematic reference spectra.

cues.narration: We study a star's evolution by examining changes in its light.
cues.visual: A schematic Sun-like star expands and reddens as the spectral peak shifts to longer wavelengths.

cues.narration: We can detect exoplanets when they pass in front of their stars and block some starlight.
cues.visual: A planet crosses the stellar disk while a light curve derived from the same overlap geometry dips and recovers.
A fixed X-ray source and schematic body produce a radiograph illustrating differential absorption.

cues.narration: and computed tomography to look inside the body.
cues.visual: The source rotates around a body cross-section with the detector opposite it; slice images appear beside it.

cues.narration: We even use microwaves to heat our food.
cues.visual: Waves inside a closed microwave oven heat a bowl of soup, producing a little steam.
